preamble: Reduction of the alveolar trill [r] to a single-contact tap [ɾ] turns several rapid tongue-tip contacts into one. It happened historically in Greek, where Ancient Greek ρ, described as a trill, is prototypically a tap in the modern language. In Polish, /r/ is traditionally classed as a trill but is realized as a tap in about 95% of intervocalic tokens, and in Italian single intervocalic /r/ is a one-contact trill, effectively a tap, while geminate /rr/ keeps several contacts.

examples.from: Ancient Greek ῥῆμα /r̥ɛ̂ː.ma/ with ρ = trill
examples.note: Ancient rho was an alveolar trill; the only Modern Greek rhotic is prototypically an alveolar tap, with a trill surviving mainly in clusters.
Recent studies find /r/ realized as a tap in about 95% of intervocalic and 80–90% of postconsonantal tokens, almost never as a trill.
Single intervocalic /r/ is realized with one or two contacts, i.e. a tap, especially in unstressed syllables, whereas geminate /rr/ keeps three to seven contacts.
